name: Capgo
tagline: Over-the-air live updates for Capacitor mobile apps, pushed without an app store review.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Capgo is open source at its core, so the DIY version is less a clone and more a self-host: the plugin already exists and you mostly need a bundle host plus an update manifest endpoint. An agent can scaffold a signed zip store, version channel logic and a tiny API in one sitting, and for a single app you control, that is genuinely enough. What you lose is everything around the hot path: staged rollouts, per-device channels, rollback when a bad bundle bricks launch, analytics on who actually installed what, and the CDN that makes a 10MB bundle download fast everywhere. There is also the uncomfortable part where shipping JS updates outside the stores lives in a grey zone that Apple tolerates only within limits, and a hosted vendor has thought harder about staying inside them than your weekend script has. Build it if you ship one app and like reading logs; pay if a bad bundle going out to real users would ruin your month.
coreLoopDIY: Builds and signs a Capacitor web bundle, uploads it to object storage, and serves a version manifest the app checks on launch to download and swap in the new bundle.
requirements: A Capacitor app you actually control and can rebuild
Object storage or any static host for bundles (S3-compatible or plain nginx)
A small always-on server or serverless function for the update manifest
Signing keypair so the app rejects bundles you did not publish
Patience for testing rollback on a real device, not just the simulator
whatYouLose: Automatic rollback when a bundle crashes on boot
Per-channel and per-device targeting for beta testers
Install analytics: who got which bundle, and who is stuck
A CDN that makes downloads fast outside your own region
Someone else tracking app store policy changes on your behalf
moatNotes: The plugin is the commodity part. The distribution, the rollback safety net and the edge delivery are the parts you notice only when they are missing.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the failure mode is brutal and silent. A self-hosted update server that serves a broken bundle takes your app down on every launch, and the only fix is a store release that takes days. Paying buys staged rollouts, a rollback button, and a CDN that does not fall over when you actually have users, which is exactly the moment self-hosting stops being fun. For a side project with fifty installs, none of that matters. For anything with revenue attached, the monthly fee is cheap insurance against a bad Tuesday.
notes: The plugin is open source, so this is one of the rare entries where self-hosting is the official path, not the hack.
prompt:
Build a minimal self-hosted over-the-air update server for a Capacitor app, plus the publish tooling around it.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Node 20 with Fastify for the API
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 for bundle metadata
- Local disk for bundle storage, with an S3-compatible adapter behind a one-file interface
- A single CLI entrypoint written as a Node script, no build step

What to build:
1. `bin/publish.js`: takes a path to a built Capacitor web dir, zips it, computes a sha256, signs the hash with an ed25519 private key from .env, uploads the zip to storage, and inserts a row (app_id, channel, version, sha256, signature, size, created_at).
2. `GET /updates/:app_id?channel=production&version=1.2.3`: returns JSON with url, version, sha256 and signature if a newer bundle exists on that channel, or 204 if the client is current. Compare versions with semver, not string sort.
3. `GET /bundles/:id`: streams the zip with an ETag and correct content-length.
4. `POST /admin/channels`: moves an existing bundle id to a channel so you can promote a beta bundle to production without re-uploading.
5. `POST /admin/rollback`: marks the current bundle on a channel as bad and re-points the channel at the previous good one.

Rules:
- Admin routes require a bearer token from ADMIN_TOKEN in .env. Everything else is public read.
- Ship a `docs/client.md` explaining how to wire @capgo/capacitor-updater or a hand-rolled fetch-and-unzip to this endpoint, including signature verification on device. Do not try to write the native side.
- Include a seed script and a test that publishes two versions and asserts the manifest, the 204, and the rollback all behave.
- No telemetry, no accounts, no analytics dashboard. One operator, one token.
- Secrets in .env only: SIGNING_KEY, ADMIN_TOKEN, optional S3_* vars. Ship .env.example.
- README must state plainly that there is no staged rollout and no crash-triggered auto-rollback, and that shipping a broken bundle will require a manual rollback call.
